{"claims":[{"claim_text":"A mortgage finance system based on competition and free enterprise should be established that is transparent, encourages the private sector to return to housing, and promotes personal responsibility on the part of borrowers.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Policies promoting reliance on private capital, like private mortgage insurance, will be critical to scaling back the federal role in the housing market and avoiding future taxpayer bailouts.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Reforms should provide clear and prudent underwriting standards and guidelines on acceptable lending practices.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Compliance with regulatory standards should provide a legal safe harbor to guard against opportunistic litigation.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac were a primary cause of the housing crisis because their implicit government guarantee allowed them to avoid market discipline and make risky investments.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The favored political status of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac enriched their politically-connected executives and their shareholders at the expense of the nation.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Both Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac should be wound down in size and scope.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Officials of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac should be held to account.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
